newsitem.title: UK: UK net mortgage lending in May rises 803 mln stg.
newsitem.headline: UK net mortgage lending in May rises 803 mln stg.

text.p: Net lending to house buyers by Britain's major banks rose by a seasonally adjusted 803 million stg in May, up from the April figure of 751 million and above the recent monthly average, the British Bankers' Association said on Friday.
The rise was the highest since January, when net lending rose by 819 million stg.

Unadjusted gross loans totalled 2.526 billion stg in May, some 7.0 percent higher than the April figure of 2.366 billion. In May 1996, there was 21 percent increase on the previous month. This series is not seasonally adjusted.
The number of net new approvals rose by 8 percent in May to 50,380 from 46,512, while their value rose to 2.913 billion stg from 2.785 billion, an increase of five percent.
In May, last year, the increases in both the volume and the value of approvals were significantly higher, at 17 percent and 18 percent respectively.

But the increase in May 1997 will have been depressed both by the fact that Easter fell in March rather than April and the boost to the April figures as customers sought fixed rate borrowing in anticipation of interest rate rises, the BBA said.

"The housing market looks set to strengthen further over the months ahead, though much will obviously depend on the future path of interest rates and decision in the forthcoming budget," Tim Sweeney, director general of the BBA said.
